- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is trending down, avoid premature bottoming — delay correction until 2–3 days after the trough.  
- Model tends to overestimate early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — apply a 3–5% downward bias to first 5–7 days.  
- If forecast shows a strong upward trend followed by a sharp drop, the model often overshoots the true decline — cap the drop to 10% below the peak.  
- When sentiment is consistently above 0.6, model tends to underestimate downward moves — add 2–3% to forecast for downward corrections.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion, model often fails to adjust — apply a 1–2% upward bias to the final 5–7 days.
